title: Sellers Rapid Embed Risk Play Cards (Draft)
summary: Pocket deck for sellers to quickly diagnose embedding risks, recommend Redwood routing/fallbacks, and close pilots. Not a polished deck — meant for booth/phone rapid-fire usage.
content:
Context and goal:
- Audience: SEs and AE sellers running short pilot discovery + embed conversations with product/platform teams (midmarket, scale-ups).
- Goal: give 6 one-page 'play cards' that map common embed risks -> quick diagnostics -> Redwood-config remedies -> trial success metrics.

Deck structure (6 cards + opener + closing):
1) Opener slide: 30s framing
   - Hook: "Embed fast, ship reliably: risk-first checklist"
   - TL;DR: Redwood provides consistent routing, KV prefix caching, and fallback chains so embeds survive spikes and reduce per-token cost.
   - Speaker note: open with a one-liner about production economics. Ask: "What are your uptime / latency must-haves for an embed?"

2) Card A - Cold-start latency on inference embeds
   - Symptoms: inconsistent first-request latency, demo-timeouts, poor UX on first users
   - Quick diag: ask about p95 cold start, model size, whether using hosted vs dedicated, batch size patterns
   - Redwood quick fixes: warm pools (Dedicated), keep-warm routing policy, prefix caching for common prompts, smaller quantized variants for tail requests
   - Pilot metric: reduce first-token latency p95 by X ms or %; success = <150ms p95 on 512 token context.
   - Script: "If you care about first-touch UX, we recommend pinning an L2 warm pool + a quantized variant for tails. Can we run a 48h smoke in dev to measure p95?"

3) Card B - High concurrency + cost shock
   - Symptoms: CPU/GPU spikes during batch ingestion, token cost surprises
   - Quick diag: ask expected concurrent users, token/session, burst patterns, budget cap
   - Redwood quick fixes: adaptive batching, autoscaled reserved pools, combinatorial routing to lower-cost variants with quality guardrails
   - Pilot metric: cost per 1k sessions and tail latency SLA.
   - Script: "We can run a 72h replay of your traffic on a Dedicated pool to show unit economics; we'll turn on adaptive batching and simulate billing delta."

4) Card C - Data residency and compliance friction for embedded model calls
   - Symptoms: Legal requests to avoid third-party processing, want VPC-only, audit logs
   - Quick diag: required region(s), retention window, redaction needs
   - Redwood quick fixes: Private deployment (VPC), customer KMS, audit log retention policy, on-prem connector for air-gapped flows
   - Pilot metric: pass security checklist + SOC doc signoff within pilot window.

5) Card D - Output drift and quality regressions after upgrade
   - Symptoms: unusual error rate, user complaints after model swap or scale change
   - Quick diag: compare eval prompts, check rollout policy (canary size), recent kernel/hardware changes
   - Redwood quick fixes: canary rollouts with eval hooks, auto-fallback to pinned version, per-prompt quality alerts in Optimize
   - Pilot metric: zero production regressions in 7-day canary; if regression observed, auto-rollback.

6) Card E - Low throughput for embedding generation (real-time feed use-case)
   - Symptoms: slow batch throughput, backlog growing, request queueing
   - Quick diag: batch window, desired latency, GPU type, payload sizes
   - Redwood quick fixes: batching policy tuning, KV cache for repeat subqueries, move to Dedicated instance sizing, model quantization tradeoff doc
   - Pilot metric: reach throughput target (e.g., 200 embeds/s) with <200ms median latency.

7) Card F - Integration platform constraints (limited HTTP timeouts, client-side SDK limitations)
   - Symptoms: client aborts, tokenized payload limits, flaky mobile networks
   - Quick diag: timeouts, retry policies, max body sizes, SDK version
   - Redwood quick fixes: streaming endpoints, resumable responses, small-chunk embedding endpoints, lightweight SDKs with backoff defaults
   - Pilot metric: integration passes synthetic mobile tests (3G emulation) and remains within client timeout budget.

Closing slide: Next steps and rapid-qualify checklist\- One page rapid qual script (3 Qs):
  1) "Do you need pinned capacity or flexible cost-first?" -> decide Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
  2) "What's your strictest latency SLO (p95) and busiest concurrency?" -> map to pool size / batching config
  3) "Any compliance restrictions or local region needs?" -> decide Private/VPC
- Pilot ask templates (choose one):
  - Quick smoke (48h): warm pool + p95 test
  - Replay & cost run (72h): run periodic traffic replay to quantify cost delta
  - Canary rollout (7d): model switch with auto-eval and rollback

Appendix (notes to self / TODOs):
- Add one-pager for legal with data flow diagram (ask security for template)
- Create three canned metrics dashboards in Console for quick hands-on demo: cold-start, cost-per-1k, embed-throughput
- Add one-liner rebuttals for common objections: "We can self-host" -> "Redwood lowers unit ops/bandwidth and gives routing/fallback primitives you have to build"; "Cost unknown" -> "We run replay and estimate within 72h"

Unresolved questions / items for follow-up:
- Need SRE input on exact warm-pool sizing defaults for G5 vs H100
- Verify Private deploy SLA wording for pilots (ask legal)

Speaker quick cheat sheet (for if you have 3min):
- 0:00 - 0:30 introduce pain + Redwood thesis (serving matters more than model)
- 0:30 - 1:30 ask 3 qual questions, pick the card that matches their pain
- 1:30 - 2:30 show the fix & pilot ask, agree on next-step (smoke/replay/canary)

Notes style: rough bullets, leave room to convert each card into a printable one-pager for booth use.

File notes: keep as a working deck — will split into 6 single-slide PDFs and one speaker notes doc when stable.
